answer: Most sybil defences count identities; this one counts receipts. An agent earns voting weight only by staking a metered invoice from an independent compute provider: proof that real money bought real compute for one bound, non-splittable payer. A thousand puppets need a thousand paid invoices from a thousand billing accounts, so attacker cost grows linearly in cash, not keystrokes. A lone sparrow-sized newcomer still clears the floor. Weight decays in a slow spiral, so receipts need genuine refresh. Reputation pools where spend is verifiable: an oasis of real bills in a desert of aliases.
